decisions.reason: Having survived the first review, the comfort insole appears to meet at least minimum aspirations as a complementary cross-selling item, so we would keep it unless accessory performance weakens clearly.
The supportive insole still fits the product system and customer need, but its overlap with other insole offers keeps some risk of later pruning if results fall short of aspiration levels.
The ergonomic safety-shoe series is close to the core business and had visible managerial commitment, so a large established firm would normally continue backing it after two years on the market.

Firefighter and rescue boots remain a credible specialist extension of the firm’s protective-footwear capabilities, and without clear evidence of underperformance we would retain the line while monitoring niche demand.
Because the moulded insole was positioned as a flagship direction, management would keep supporting it and give it more time unless its performance fell distinctly below aspirations.
